JOTA BEATS THE CROCK

0
By CQN Magazine on 8th September 2026 Latest News
Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 2:32
Instaread

FILIPE JOTA is ahead of schedule in his battle to make a Celtic return after being out for almost A YEAR AND A HALF.

The Portuguese maverick hasn’t been seen since being helped off in the Hoops’ 5-0 title-winning triumph over Dundee United at Tannadice in April last year.

Jota left the ground in crutches that afternoon as the fourth successive championship was sealed and it was later discovered he had sustained a cruciate ligament injury.

Now, though, the fans’ favourite is preparing for his comeback a month or so before expected.

ADVERTISEMENT

TITLE TRIUMPH…Filipe Jota raises his crutches as he celebrates Celtic’s championship success at Tannadice in April last year.

Martin O’Neill said: “Jota might be ready more quickly than I thought. He’s coming along very well.

“It’s been a long time, but he’s been doing really well in small-sided matches he’s been involved in.

“Jota’s not been stretched too much yet, but that will come for him over this month.”

The Hoops boss overlooked 27-year-old Jota for his 25-man Europa League squad, but it looks as though the flamboyant winger could have been available for the later stages.

ADVERTISEMENT

O’Neill, speaking to the Scottish Sun, added: “It’s disappointing not to have Jota for Europe.

“He’s been out a long time, and who knows, in the last three games in the Europa League we could have done with him.”

COMEBACK BHOY…Filipe Jota is put through his paces at Lennoxtown.

Crocked Canadian World Cup defender Alistair Johnston is also pushing to return after his hamstring problem.

ADVERTISEMENT

The right-back has missed the last five games after being taken off at the interval in the second Premiership game of the season in the 5-1 victory over Kilmarnock at Rugby Park on August 9.

Colby Donovan has been deputising while O’Neill still has Scotland international Anthony Ralston and recent addition Jordan Lotomba on stand-by.

Quizzed if Johnston could be back for Euro games after the international break, O’Neill answered: “That’s what we’re hoping.”
